titulo: Brand film from your own site
lead: So far the video became a page. Now the reverse path: the page becomes a video. filmarca (ARCKHÉ) reads the colors, fonts, logo, copy, and screenshots of a site and builds a brand film in HyperFrames. You run the whole path against the kit's page without calling any model, using filmarca's own template scenes, and then you put the film on the page.
objetivo: read the kit site's DNA with filmarca and render a brand film with template scenes, without calling a model.

aprende.t: The DNA: what filmarca reads from a site and where it gets it wrong
A script built from facts on the page and the six template scenes (opening, title, number, screenshot, list, call to action)
Local render, no model: the rehearsal that proves the path before you spend anything
The film back on the page, without weighing down the first paint

hero_alt: Two monitors on a dark desk: on the left a page with color swatches, on the right a video timeline; a closed clapperboard on the desk.

nos.detalhe: Opens the site in a headless Chromium and writes marca.json: colors by role (background, text, primary), fonts, logo, headlines, numbers, and screenshots of the top, of three strips, and of the phone view. No model.
The director (the model on your subscription, through claude -p or codex exec) writes the concept and the scenes using only facts from marca.json. In the rehearsal, you write roteiro.json by hand.

Each scene becomes HTML, CSS, and GSAP under a closed contract. The check runs each scene in all three formats and rejects network calls, clocks, randomness, CSS animation, text outside the frame, and split words. Rejected twice, the template scene takes its place.
One composition per language and format (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), lint, and an MP4 rendered on your machine.
The MP4 goes into a regular section, with preload="none" and a poster: it does not weigh down the first paint and only downloads when the person presses play.

secoes.volta: the film goes back to the site
secoes.legenda: filmarca pins hyperframes 0.8.134 in its package-lock (10/19/2026); course 3 teaches 0.8.176. Use the project's lock: it's the one its tests passed on.

secoes.sub: In a rehearsal folder, at the tested commit. The project's npm test runs without a model.

blocos.conteudo:
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-sites/a5; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E"; cd "$E"
git clone -q https://github.com/linnoff88-dev/filmarca && cd filmarca && git checkout -q 0c0356c; echo "clone: $?"
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund > npm.log 2>&1; echo "npm ci: $?"
node -p "'hyperframes ' + require('hyperframes/package.json').version + ' · playwright ' + require('playwright/package.json').version"
npx playwright install chromium > pw.log 2>&1; echo "chromium: $?"
npm test 2>&1 | grep -E "^ℹ (pass|fail)"

abas.html:
clone: 0
npm ci: 0
hyperframes 0.8.134 · playwright 1.63.0
chromium: 0
ℹ pass 5
ℹ fail 0

The 5 tests prove that a broken scene is rejected and that the template scene takes its place.

secoes.titulo: Read the DNA of the kit's page
secoes.sub: The kit's server serves the lens page; filmarca reads it the way it would read any site.

blocos.rot: Terminal · DNA of the kit's site
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cARCKHÉ-ia-sites-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-sites/a5; cd "$E/filmarca"
node "$K/scripts/servir.mjs" "$K/site" > "$E/url.txt" & S=$!
until U=$(cat "$E/url.txt") && [ -n "$U" ] && curl -s -o /dev/null "$U"; do sleep 0.3; done
node bin/filmarca.mjs dna "$U" --out "$E/filme"; echo "dna: $?"
kill $S
ls "$E/filme/assets"

abas.html:
lendo http://127.0.0.1:<porta>/
  marca: Aurora 35 · cores #0c0c10 #f3efe7 #e2a23b #e2a23b #0b0b0d · fontes Georgia / system-ui · logo assets/logo.svg
dna: 0
fonts
logo.svg
print-1.png
print-2.png
print-3.png
print-celular.png
print-topo.png

Note the primary color: #e2a23b is the yellow of the motion switch (Parado / Ligado), not the brand's accent. The DNA reads what shows on screen. Check marca.json before you generate, and fix by hand whatever is wrong.

secoes.sub: A script built from facts on the page (kit/filmarca/roteiro.json) and filmarca's template scenes in place of the scenes step.

blocos.rot: Terminal · template scenes, render, and check
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cARCKHÉ-ia-sites-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-sites/a5; cd "$E/filmarca"
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1
cp "$K/filmarca/roteiro.json" "$E/filme/"
node "$K/scripts/cenas-modelo.mjs" . "$E/filme"
node bin/filmarca.mjs render "$E/filme" --formatos 16x9 --rascunho; echo "render: $?"
python3 "$K/scripts/conferir-video.py" "$E/filme/renders/aurora-35-pt-16x9.mp4" 17.5 1920x1080; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
cenas-modelo: 5 cenas · 17,5 s · marca Aurora 35 · logo assets/logo.svg
  ✓ renders/aurora-35-pt-16x9.mp4 · 8 s (lint com avisos)
/tmp/ensaio-sites/a5/filme/renders/aurora-35-pt-16x9.mp4
render: 0
OK: 17,5 s · 1920×1080 · 30 fps · sem áudio
saída: 0

Five scenes, 17.5 s, draft render in seconds. "lint com avisos" is a warning, not an error: the MP4 came out and passed the checker.

secoes.titulo: With the model from your subscription, and back on the page
secoes.sub: The real step swaps the hand-written script and the template scenes for the director and the scenes animated by the model. Then the MP4 goes into the page.

blocos.rot: With the model · script, scenes, and render
blocos.conteudo:
cd <pasta-do-filmarca>
node bin/filmarca.mjs roteiro <pasta-do-filme> --pedido "filme de apresentaçêo da lente para a página" --motor claude
node bin/filmarca.mjs cenas <pasta-do-filme> --motor claude
node bin/filmarca.mjs render <pasta-do-filme> --formatos 16x9,9x16 --rascunho
A Aurora 35 em 17 segundos

exercicios.titulo: E3 · The film on the page
exercicios.texto: In a copy of the kit's page, create the filme/ folder, copy the MP4, and grab the poster (ffmpeg -ss 2 -i filme/aurora-35-pt-16x9.mp4 -frames:v 1 filme/poster.jpg). Paste the section from kit/exemplos/video-da-marca.html before the spec sheet and run peso.py with --inicial 0.5.
exercicios.pronto: peso.py shows vídeo on the PESO line and primeira pintura … DENTRO.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: Which filmarca step runs with no model at all?
perguntas.explica: The dna is Playwright reading the page: colors, fonts, logo, texts, and screenshots. Script, scenes, and translation use the model from your subscription; in the rehearsal, the script is hand-written and the scenes are the template scenes.

perguntas.p: The DNA returned the primary color #e2a23b, which is the color of the motion key. What do you do?
opcoes: Run the dna until it gets it right.
Delete the motion key from the site.
Generate the film anyway; the model notices the wrong color and fixes it on its own.
Check marca.json and fix the color by hand before generating.
perguntas.explica: The DNA reads what shows on screen, and a colored button counts as a color. marca.json is yours: fixing one line costs less than redoing scenes.

perguntas.p: A scene written by the model was rejected twice by the check. What does filmarca do?
opcoes: It puts the template scene of the same type in its place.
It publishes the rejected scene with a warning.
It asks the model for a third, a fourth, and a fifth attempt.
perguntas.explica: Once rejected, the model fixes it one time; if it fails again, the template scene steps in. The film always comes out, and the review page shows which scene is a template.

perguntas.p: Why does the brand video go into the page with preload="none"?
opcoes: Because without preload="none" the video doesn't play on phones in any browser.
Because GitHub Pages doesn't serve large MP4s.
So the MP4 only downloads when the person asks, outside the first paint.
So the video plays on its own when the page opens.
perguntas.explica: With preload="none" and a poster, the browser only downloads the video on play. The first paint stays the same; peso.py counts the video in the total, not at the start.

itens.texto: filmarca reads the site without a model; check marca.json.
Handwritten script + template scenes + local render = a film without spending anything.
MP4 with a poster and preload="none" in a section of the page.
